findings.currentDescriptionDe: Die lernende Person kann die Reaktivität von Carbonsäurechloriden, Carbonsäureanhydriden und Carbonsäureestern bei vergleichbaren nucleophilen Acylsubstitutionen ordnen und die Unterschiede anhand von Carbonylgruppe und Abgangsgruppe begründen.
findings.currentDescriptionEn: The learner can rank the reactivity of carboxylic acid chlorides, carboxylic acid anhydrides, and carboxylic esters in comparable nucleophilic acyl substitutions and justify the differences using the carbonyl group and leaving group.
requiredAspects: three specified derivative families: acid chlorides, acid anhydrides and carboxylic esters
ranking under comparable nucleophilic acyl-substitution conditions
findings.strongestPrimaryContext: The complete single RP p40 table and optional enrichment box, interpreted using RP pp19-21 table grammar and pp12/13/15 general modelling, controlled-comparison, data and argument operations.
findings.legitimateBoundedAuthorInference: Addition-elimination necessarily gives the entering nucleophile and departing group a role in a selected acyl-substitution case. The same course page explicitly permits optional acid chloride/anhydride examples and carbonyl-activity/rate reasoning. A carefully controlled derivative comparison is therefore a coherent author teaching extension of this local context; missing literal words alone do not disqualify it.
findings.unresolvedBridge: The prescribed generic mechanism and optional carbonyl-activity statement do not establish how differences in both carbonyl activation and leaving-group behavior determine the rank across all three families. No original comparison model/data specifying that full operation was found in the bounded primary contexts inspected. Adding this comparison from general chemical knowledge would still be an author subject-content commitment, not demonstrated official whole-goal evidence.
findings.courseAndOptionalityLimit: Any future RP route must explicitly retain the grey optional enrichment semantics and LK mechanism dependency. It cannot be relabeled compulsory RP LK, Hessen LK or all current jurisdictions.
findings.nextSpecificEvidenceNeeded: One genuine original relevant course/model context that makes this complete controlled three-family reactivity comparison (including both justifications) a faithful operationalization, or an independent explicit decision accepting the documented RP same-page bridge while preserving optionality. Mere locator repair, source-target hash refresh or generic operator union cannot resolve the hold.

findings.currentDescriptionDe: Die lernende Person kann die intramolekulare Esterbildung aus vorgegebenen Hydroxycarbonsäuren anhand von Strukturformeln erklären und Bildungstendenz sowie relative Stabilität der entstehenden Lactone unter angegebenen Bedingungen anhand von Ringstruktur und Vergleichsdaten begründen.
findings.currentDescriptionEn: The learner can explain intramolecular ester formation from specified hydroxycarboxylic acids using structural formulas and justify the formation tendency and relative stability of the resulting lactones under stated conditions using ring structure and comparative data.
requiredAspects: intramolecular ester formation from specified hydroxycarboxylic acids
justification using ring structure and comparative data
findings.strongestPrimaryContext: Current HE pp39/40 Q1.3 combines hydroxycarboxylic-acid structure, ester formation/condensation, structural formulas and the ester-synthesis mechanism in one topic. ST ester addition-elimination and BY drug ester/amide condensation provide alternative complete model contexts, each with its own course boundary.
findings.legitimateBoundedAuthorInference: Applying familiar ester bond formation to hydroxy and carboxy groups on the same specified molecule can be a coherent intramolecular transfer case. This is an author inference, not a literal prescribed lactone/ring-closure statement. Provided comparative data can bound the result and prevent a universal ring-size claim.
findings.unresolvedBridge: Ring closure alone does not establish the full second operation: justifying formation tendency and relative stability from ring structure and comparison data under stated conditions. None of the inspected complete original contexts supplies the corresponding ring/comparison model or dedicated lactone context. General ester formation, molecule geometry, equilibrium/data operators, ascorbic-acid structure or prerequisite mastery do not fill that missing whole-goal demand by themselves.
findings.courseAndOptionalityLimit: The current LK tag and nine inherited jurisdiction labels are not direct whole-goal source evidence. Separate source-context fragments may not be pooled to fabricate a complete scoped goal claim.
findings.nextSpecificEvidenceNeeded: A genuine original relevant course/model context for intramolecular hydroxycarboxylic-acid ester rings together with the required condition-dependent formation/stability comparison. Keep the whole current goal and hold until that evidence is reviewed; no easier hydroxyacid recognition replacement is proposed.

absenceClaimBoundary: The result is a bounded investigation of the named actual contexts, not a proof of absence from every page, curriculum, official exam or possible original source.
